column2: req_desc

Published pages and titles
Every address in the site map answers HTTP 200 with its full page and document title on a direct load, and every other page address answers 404 with its not-found heading.

Header, skip link and current page
Every page starts with the `Skip to content` link and has the fixed header, showing the `Main` navigation or the `Menu` button depending on width, and marks exactly the current section's link as current.

Footer and illustrative contact
Every page ends with the footer carrying the fictional-studio notice, the footer and social navigations and the illustrative contact details.

Opening scene
The home page opens on the three-line intro heading, and `Enter the worlds` moves to world 1, focuses its rail button, announces it and runs the descent onto the ring.

Published stage state
The stage publishes its mode, active world, rendered yaw, target yaw, camera state and emblem angle as data attributes that always agree with the overlay, rail and announcer and read as published in each mode.

Immersive entry journey
A founder opens the site, enters the worlds, enters and leaves Ledgerwick Advisory, and moves forward and back through history with the same address, focus and camera states each time.

Entering and leaving a world
Entering a world changes the address, title, content and focus in one step and flies the camera in, and leaving restores the same active world, scroll position and focus on its enter button.

World-to-world links
A world page's previous and next world links move to the neighbouring world in ring order without wrapping, updating address, focus, active world and target yaw together.

World rail and keys
The world rail has one Tab stop and marks the active world. It selects worlds by click, tap, arrow keys, Home and End, and `Previous world` and `Next world` are disabled at the ends.

Ring turn
Every change of active world turns the ring straight from its rendered yaw to the new target in the published time, with the yaw moving in one direction and reaching the target exactly.

Pointer drag
Dragging anywhere on the stage outside its buttons, links and rail turns the ring with the pointer, up to one world either side. Releasing after the published distance selects the next or previous world, and nothing is selected past the ends.

3D world navigation journey
A founder drags, clicks the rail and follows world links in the 3D stage and sees the active world, yaw, overlay and scroll position agree at every step, also with reduced motion.

Scroll selects the world
On the home page the scroll position alone decides the active world, one world per viewport height, and every other way of selecting a world moves the scroll position to match.

Reversed scroll mid-turn
A new active world during a turn starts a fresh turn from the yaw shown at that moment, so reversing the scroll mid-turn settles on the world the scroll position names.

World announcer
The `World announcer` live region reads the published world line exactly once per change of active world and when `Enter the worlds` brings world 1 in, never on load, never as a repeat and never while scrolling within one world's range, as qualified in Feedback states.

Scroll-driven journey
A founder scrolls through, back and past the ring on desktop and tablet and sees one announcement and one turn per distinct world reached.

Keyboard-only journey
A founder walks the ring, enters and leaves a world, and opens a case study and its image viewer using only the keyboard, with focus always visible and returned to each opener.

Visible focus clear of the header
Every keyboard focus shows the published focus ring, and every keyboard or scripted focus move scrolls its element clear of the fixed header and into view only when it is not already there, while a pointer click alone never scrolls.

Reduced motion
With reduced motion every turn, descent, flight and slide completes in the step that starts it and no animation runs, while every control, key, address, announcement and focus move still works.

Reduced-motion journey
A founder with reduced motion reaches all eight worlds and their pages through the rail and sees instant state changes in the stage, viewer and menu.

Idle emblem motion
In 3D mode each island's emblem turns at the published steady rate as the stage's only idle motion, and holds still with reduced motion.

Scene models
Each world's model is a binary glTF file with at least 5,000 vertices served from the studio's file store, and the stage fetches all eight on first load of the home page or a world page.

Still layout without WebGL
Without WebGL the worlds section shows its heading, notice and eight world cards in ring order with links to every world page in place of the overlay, rail and stage buttons, and world pages work without a canvas.

Scene failure and retry
When any scene model fails, the same still layout appears with its notice and `Try 3D again`, which returns to 3D with world 1 active and focused once all eight models load.

3D fallback journey
A founder without WebGL, with a failing model, or with the file store unreachable still reaches every world's text, images or image plates and links, and can still send the enquiry.

Files and file-store outage
Scene and gallery files stream from the private bucket under their published keys. Unknown files answer 404, every file answers 503 while the file store is unreachable, and failed images show their plate.

World pages
Each world page shows the world's own ground, ink and display face and its published content in the published order.

Services tabs
The `Services` tab list selects services by click, tap, arrow keys, Home and End, keeps the address on `/services/<id>`, and selects the addressed service on a direct load.

Service panels and process steps
Each service panel shows its purpose, deliverables, four collapsible process steps, examples and its work, price and enquiry links.

Service exploration journey
A marketing lead compares services by keyboard, opens process steps and follows a service's enquiry link to an enquiry with that service already chosen.

Work filters and counts
The work gallery filters by service and industry together, using the published matching rule, counts and results status.

Show more work
The gallery shows the published page size of matching projects in gallery order, and `Show more work` appends the next page with focus on its first tile, never repeating or skipping a project.

Gallery address and return
Filters and pages live in the gallery address, loading the address restores them, and returning from a case study lands on the same address with focus on the opened tile.

Projects API paging
`GET /api/projects` filters like the gallery and pages by offset with a capped limit, giving every match once in gallery order.

Portfolio filtering journey
A founder combines service and industry filters, pages with Show more, opens a case study and comes back to the same filters, page and tile.

Case studies
Each case study shows its published sections in order, previous and next project links that wrap in gallery order, and its world and gallery links.

Image viewer
The gallery's modal `Image viewer` changes images by buttons, arrow keys and swipe, wrapping at the ends, keeps Tab inside, and returns focus to its thumbnail on close.

Case-study navigation journey
A founder moves between case studies, browses a gallery by keyboard and by touch at phone width, and returns to the filtered gallery they came from.

Price list items
The price list shows the fourteen illustrative items with type, price, delivery and revisions, and each item's details expand to its inclusions, payment line and enquiry link.

Price filters and counts
The `Category` and `Price type` radio groups filter the price list together, with the published counts, status, empty state and address.

Pricing journey
A marketing lead filters the price list by keyboard, opens an item's details, reloads to the same filters and follows the item's enquiry link to step 2.

Studio page
The studio page shows the published principles, people, project stages and links, with the principles in two columns on desktop and one on a phone.

Questions
The questions page lists the eight questions as an accordion operated by click, tap, Enter, Space and arrow keys, and opens the question named in the address on load.

Enquiry steps and draft
The four-step enquiry moves focus to each step's heading, never changes an answer on Back or Edit, and restores answers and step from this tab's draft.

Enquiry validation
Next checks every field of the step against the published rules and messages, marks invalid fields and radio groups and focuses the first one (a radio group by its first radio).

Multi-step enquiry journey
A marketing lead fills in, corrects, reloads and reviews the enquiry and sees every answer kept exactly as typed.

Enquiry request checks
`POST /api/enquiries` refuses wrong content types, oversized bodies, invalid JSON and invalid fields with the published statuses and bodies, and ignores unpublished fields.

Intake hand-off
Each new enquiry is stored and handed to the project-intake service once, and is shown as sent only with the intake reference that service returned, as qualified in Business rules.

One enquiry per submission
Repeated or simultaneous posts with one submission id store one enquiry with one reference, and a retry after a failed hand-off sends the stored enquiry again.

Enquiry limit per email
New enquiries from one email address beyond the published number within the published window are refused with 429, the wait time and the published alert, and nothing is stored.

Enquiry error and success journey
A marketing lead meets the length, intake-failure and limit refusals, retries and reaches the sent panel with both references, while the studio receives one enquiry per send.

Only the published surface
Every path, file and method outside the published pages, files and API answers the published 404 or 405, and no error reveals server internals.

Responsive layout and touch targets
At the three published widths every page fits without horizontal scrolling and follows the published layout, and on a phone every control is at least 44 by 44 pixels.

Menu dialog
Below 1024 pixels wide `Menu` opens a modal menu that keeps Tab inside, closes by Escape, `Close menu`, a tap outside or a link, and returns focus to `Menu`.

Mobile and accessibility journey
A marketing lead on a 375-pixel phone uses the menu, swipes and scrolls through the worlds by touch and meets no serious accessibility findings, also with reduced motion.

Deployment and health
The app installs, builds and serves from its run manifest on the published port and answers the health check as published.

Configuration from the environment
Every service address, credential and setting is read from the published environment variables at start and is never hard-coded or sent to the browser.

Gallery-dark editorial look
The studio's own pages show the deep ink ground, warm paper text, gold accent, high-contrast serif headlines and quiet sans body at an airy measure.

Distinct world art direction
The eight world islands and pages read as eight different brands through their own colours, type and island forms.

Real 3D stage
The stage is a real WebGL scene rendered from the served models, with no pre-rendered video or image standing in for it.
/app/run.json is a JSON object with exactly the string keys _schema (value run-manifest-v1), install, build and serve.
THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md at /app lists every shipped package (the production dependency tree from npm ls --omit=dev --all --json) and every font file with its licence.
Every shipped package (the production dependency tree from npm ls --omit=dev --all --json) uses MIT, ISC, BSD-2-Clause, BSD-3-Clause, Apache-2.0 or 0BSD, and every font file uses SIL OFL 1.1.
The app stores data only in the provided Postgres database and MinIO bucket: no SQLite, no other database or cache, and no data files written as storage.
The provided development compose files and service configuration stay unchanged.
Application source is TypeScript; plain JavaScript appears only in build or tool configuration files.
No page or stylesheet references a font, script, image or other asset on another host.
